hook: The police want to arrest me without a warrant.

slides.title: Yes, in certain cases.
slides.body: A police officer can arrest without a warrant or a Magistrate's order in cases the law lists, such as when someone commits a cognizable offence in front of them.

slides.title: Accused, not caught in the act? Arrest must be necessary.
slides.body: If you're accused of a cognizable offence punishable with up to 7 years, police can arrest only if they have reason to believe you did it and arrest is necessary. Reasons must be recorded in writing.

slides.title: "Necessary" means, for example:
list: To stop threats or pressure on witnesses
When your presence in court can't otherwise be ensured

slides.title: Otherwise, you get a notice to appear.
slides.body: If arrest isn't required, police must give you a notice to appear before them. If you comply, you shall not be arrested for that offence unless police record reasons why you should be.

slides.title: Ignore the notice, and you can be arrested.
slides.body: If you don't comply with the notice, or refuse to identify yourself, police may arrest you for the offence in the notice.

slides.title: Over 60 or infirm? Extra protection.
slides.body: If you are infirm or above 60, and the offence is punishable with less than 3 years, police need prior permission from an officer of DSP rank or above to arrest you.

slides.title: If arrested, you must be told why.
slides.body: Police must tell you the full grounds of arrest at once, inform a relative, friend or person you name, and, unless the offence is non-bailable, tell you that you can get bail.

caption:
Can the police arrest you without a warrant? Here's what the law says. 👇

1️⃣ Yes, in cases the law lists, like a cognizable offence committed in front of them
2️⃣ Accused (not caught in the act) of a cognizable offence with up to 7 years' jail? Arrest must be necessary, with reasons in writing
3️⃣ If it isn't, you get a notice to appear. Comply, and you shall not be arrested unless police record why
4️⃣ Infirm or over 60, offence under 3 years? Police need prior permission from a DSP or above
5️⃣ If arrested, you must be told the grounds, and someone you name must be informed

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 35, 47, 48
